notes:
Describes a pattern of intersecting horizontal and vertical lines forming squares or rectangles. The term covers everything from fabric plaids to architectural lattice designs to chess boards.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {格子模様|こうしもよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{布|ぬの}→布：01489_nuno⟧: checkered fabric
- {格子模様|こうしもよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ネクタイ→ネクタイ：01040_nekutai⟧: plaid necktie
- ⟦{細|こま}かい→細かい：01245_komakai⟧{格子模様|こうしもよう}: fine grid pattern

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦チェック→チェック：03000_chekku⟧⟦{柄|がら}→柄：02609_gara⟧: check pattern (loanword; very common in fashion contexts)
- ⟦{市松模様|いちまつもよう}→市松模様：30129_ichimatsumoyou⟧: checkerboard pattern (traditional Japanese term; alternating colored squares like a chessboard)
- ⟦{縞模様|しまもよう}→縞模様：26237_shimamoyou⟧: stripe pattern (lines running in one direction only)
- {格子|こうし}: lattice, grid (the structural element itself, without ⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {格子|こうし} (lattice) is a significant motif in Japanese culture, seen in traditional wooden window screens (⟦{格子窓|こうしまど}→格子窓：24367_koushimado⟧), shop fronts, and textile patterns. The related ⟦{市松模様|いちまつもよう}→市松模様：30129_ichimatsumoyou⟧ gained worldwide recognition as the design motif for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
